HTTP Resource Resolve Behavior

withHttpResourceBehavior is a resolve behavior that normalizes Angular HttpResourceRef<T> inputs by observing the resource’s reactive value signal and extracting a resolved value for downstream pipeline processing.

This behavior operates exclusively in the Resolve stage and is available only when using . It affects how an incoming HTTP resource is resolved, never when it enters the pipeline or how it is later processed.

State updates participate in this behavior when a HttpResourceRef<T> is supplied as the incoming state value. The Resolve stage detects the resource input, subscribes to its reactive value signal, and resolves the first available concrete value for pipeline execution.

withHttpResourceBehavior is a pipeline-critical resolve behavior in Angular environments. When enabled via the experimental HTTP resource flag, loading and error signals emitted by the resource are synchronized with the pipeline, and resolution failures are normalized and propagated deterministically.

Diagrams
Configuration

withHttpResourceBehavior requires no explicit configuration parameters at the behavior level. It is installed automatically as part of the Resolve stage when running under and participates conditionally based on the incoming state input type.

This behavior activates when a state update is supplied with an Angular HttpResourceRef<T> input. During resolution, the Resolve stage detects the resource reference, bridges its reactive value signal into an observable, and resolves the first available concrete value for downstream pipeline processing.

withHttpResourceBehavior is pipeline-critical in Angular environments and cannot be disabled when the experimental HTTP resource feature is enabled. Loading and error signals emitted by the resource are synchronized with the pipeline, while resolution failures are normalized and propagated deterministically.

HTTP resource resolution is gated behind an experimental feature flag. When the flag is disabled or when the incoming input is not a HttpResourceRef, this behavior does not participate and resolution proceeds through other applicable resolve behaviors.

Examples

withHttpResourceBehavior participates automatically in Angular environments when a HttpResourceRef<T> is supplied as a state input. No explicit configuration is required during FeatureCell initialization.

In the example below, a FeatureCell is initialized normally. After initialization, an Angular HTTP resource is created and submitted using replaceState. The Resolve stage detects the HttpResourceRef, observes its reactive value signal, and resolves the first available value before downstream pipeline processing occurs.

Example 1: Resolve an Angular HttpResourceRef State Update

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor(private readonly http: HttpClient) {
    this.vault.initialize();

    // Create an Angular HTTP resource
    const employeesResource = this.http.resource`}}<Employee[]>{{`('/api/employees');

    // Submit the HttpResourceRef as a state update
    this.vault.replaceState(employeesResource);
  }
}`}}
